record.title: Google DeepMind and Artificial Analysis introduce a benchmark for multimodal knowledge agents
record.summary: A Nov 10 technical report introduces the Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark: 200 private, multi-file professional tasks spanning 10 sectors and 83 occupations, plus 10 disjoint public showcase tasks. The tasks require agents to combine visually dense files and often produce standalone deliverables. The authors evaluate four frontier models in a common Stirrup harness and report that removing image viewing lowered Gemini 4 Carbon’s Climb-WSR by 5.94 percentage points while increasing turns and output tokens. Reported quality differences among the top three models were statistically indistinguishable; model scores and cost estimates remain paper-reported.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Google DeepMind published a dated technical report introducing MKA on 2026-11-10, with a separate 10-task public showcase and an Artificial Analysis-hosted leaderboard.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The report says MKA contains 200 private professional tasks across 10 sectors and 83 occupations, with 2–45 input files per task; 88% require standalone deliverables. Four frontier models were run in Stirrup v0.2.1 under a common tool set and resource budget.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In a 50-task, 9-sector study, the report says its sandboxed agentic autorater achieved 96.2% weighted pairwise criterion agreement with human raters (95% CI 94.7–97.6; Cohen’s κ=0.91). The study filtered toward high-weight criteria and a balanced pass/fail mix; this agreement may not transfer to lower-weight formatting checks.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The report says Fable 5.2, Gemini 4 Carbon and Opus 5.5 were statistically indistinguishable on Climb-WSR in this evaluation; Carbon used 5.74× fewer tokens and had 6.26× lower list-price API cost than Fable 5.2. Removing image viewing from Carbon reduced Climb-WSR by 5.94 percentage points and increased turns by 1.28×. These are report results, not independent measurements.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The report does not establish that MKA scores predict performance across professional work outside these tasks, or that the autorater agreement generalizes to every criterion or population. Each model ran once per task and received one autorater pass, so run-to-run agent and grader variance are not captured; the private task set was not independently inspected here.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent rerun of MKA scores or inspection of task-level outputs was conducted; the 200-task evaluation set is private.
Each model was run once/task and graded in one autorater pass, so run-to-run agent and grader variance are not captured.
Human-rater agreement was tested on 50 tasks and weighted toward high-weight criteria; transfer to low-weight formatting checks is uncertain.

brief.importance_rationale: If the benchmark and rater methodology hold beyond the reported sample, it adds a realistic, multi-file evaluation surface for visual knowledge-work agents and can change model and tool-design choices. Score 5 reflects meaningful evaluation infrastructure; the benchmark does not establish broad deployment capability.
limitations: The 200 evaluation tasks are private; only 10 disjoint showcase tasks are downloadable.
Each model runs once per task and receives one autorater pass; confidence intervals cover task sampling but not run-to-run agent or grader variance.
The human agreement study covers 50 tasks across 9 sectors and focuses on high-weight criteria with a balanced pass/fail mix; agreement may not transfer to low-weight formatting checks.
The vision ablation is performed only on Gemini 4 Carbon.
The sandbox has internet access, so some information may be retrieved online rather than extracted visually.
API cost estimates use provider list prices at report time and may change; they are not invoices or total deployment costs.
The report is by Google DeepMind, and Artificial Analysis is a benchmark partner and leaderboard host; the research desk did not independently reproduce the results.

relationships.summary: MKA is the benchmark used in a dated evaluation of Gemini 4 Carbon; the benchmark and model rollout are separate events.

brief.summary: A Nov 10 technical report introduces the Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark: 200 private, multi-file professional tasks spanning 10 sectors and 83 occupations, plus 10 disjoint public showcase tasks. The tasks require agents to combine visually dense files and often produce standalone deliverables. The authors evaluate four frontier models in a common Stirrup harness and report that removing image viewing lowered Gemini 4 Carbon’s Climb-WSR by 5.94 percentage points while increasing turns and output tokens. Reported quality differences among the top three models were statistically indistinguishable; model scores and cost estimates remain paper-reported.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report a 200-task evaluation, a 50-task rater comparison and benchmark results for four frontier models, with a visual-tool ablation for Gemini 4 Carbon.
technical.compute_or_cost: Paper reports provider list-price estimates: $5.63/task for Gemini 4 Carbon and $35.28/task for Claude Fable 5.2 in this harness. These are author-calculated and price-sensitive, not measured invoices.
technical.demonstrated_result: The dated paper and public showcase establish that the benchmark was published. No independent benchmark result is demonstrated in this record.
technical.implementation_status: Published benchmark and leaderboard; task set is private, with 10 public showcase tasks.
technical.mechanism: A standardized tool-using agent processes heterogeneous visually dense inputs and creates standalone files; an agentic grader renders and inspects outputs against weighted, expert-authored criteria.
technical.novelty: Combines multi-file visual reasoning, tool use and graded standalone deliverables across professional workflows; unlike some text-heavy benchmarks, its Carbon image-viewing ablation measures a visual-tool contribution.
technical.regime: Private 200-task benchmark across 10 sectors and 83 occupations; 10 disjoint public showcase tasks; 2–45 input files/task; each model run once per task in an internet-enabled sandbox with up to 250 turns and 8 hours.
technical.reproducibility: 10 showcase tasks and open Stirrup harness are public; private evaluation set and task-level trajectories are not available here. No independent rerun performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: Within the paper, four models share Stirrup v0.2.1, tools, sandbox and budgets. The top three reported Climb-WSR estimates are statistically indistinguishable; cross-benchmark superiority is not established.

brief.title: Google DeepMind and Artificial Analysis introduce a benchmark for multimodal knowledge agents
brief.why_it_matters: MKA targets a gap between single-image QA, text-heavy agent benchmarks and real work that combines visual files with finished documents, spreadsheets or presentations. Its task design and tool ablation can help researchers distinguish native visual reasoning from code/OCR workarounds. The private evaluation set limits outside auditing, and the reported scores do not establish general workplace performance.

other.title: Google opens Gemini 4 Carbon to broader developer, enterprise and research access
other.summary: On Nov. 10 Google announced broader access to Gemini 4 Carbon, following an Oct. 28 rollout initially limited to selected cyber defenders. The new post says paid developers and enterprises can use it through the Gemini API, Google AI Studio and business products; Google AI Ultra subscribers are receiving access in Antigravity, the Gemini app and Search. Google also expanded a research-access program. The post reports broad gains in coding, cybersecurity and scientific reasoning, but its benchmark and application claims remain provider-reported. This review did not verify a successful API call, access by region, or the linked Carbon-specific model card; no independent matched-harness reproduction was performed.
